title: A REAL-TIME SYSTEM FOR EPILEPTIC SEIZURE PREDICTION AND METHOD THEREOF
abstract: ABSTRACT A REAL-TIME SYSTEM FOR EPILEPTIC SEIZURE PREDICTION AND METHOD THEREOF The present invention relates to a real-time system for early prediction of epileptic seizures from scalp electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. The system acquires multi-channel EEG at ≥ 256 Hz, performs digital filtering and sliding-window segmentation, and derives time-, frequency- and wavelet-domain features. A hybrid neural network—comprising separable 1-D convolutions, squeeze-and-excitation blocks, multi-head self-attention and residual connections—classifies each window as pre-ictal or inter-ictal. Quantised to 8-bit precision and pruned to ≤ 720 kB, the model executes on a Typhoon HIL C2000 microcontroller with 0.1–1 s latency and 50–100 mW power. The system of the present invention attains ≥ 99 % accuracy, sensitivity and specificity on CHB-MIT and Siena datasets, issuing actionable alerts at least five seconds before seizure onset to enable continuous bedside or wearable monitoring.

title: A System and Method for Epileptic Seizure Detection and Adaptive Neurostimulation
abstract: The present disclosure proposes a system (100) for epileptic seizure detection and adaptive neurostimulation. The system (100) is configured to autonomously monitor physiological signals, detect seizure conditions, and deliver adaptive neurostimulation in a closed-loop manner. The system (100) comprises at least one energy harvesting unit (102), an energy storage unit (104), a control unit (106), and a neurostimulation interface configured for therapeutic delivery. The system (100) is configured to operate without continuous external power supply or internet connectivity and may be implemented as a wearable or implantable medical device enclosed within a sealed biocompatible housing. The system (100) is configured to harvest electrical energy from ambient sources including body heat, kinetic motion, and ambient light, thereby enabling continuous operation without reliance on external power supply or frequent battery replacement.

title: A SYSTEM AND METHOD FOR REDUCING THE FOOTPRINT OF SEIZURE PREDICTION SYSTEM USING ELECTROCARDIOGRAM
abstract: The present disclosure provides a wearable electrocardiogram-based seizure prediction system (100) and a method (200) for predicting seizures from single-channel electrocardiogram signals. The system (100) includes a wearable sensor (102) acquiring electrocardiogram signals, a preprocessing unit (104) denoising and segmenting the signals into frames, a spectral whitening unit (106) modelling a whitening filter from interictal frames to generate residual electrocardiogram signals, and a cepstral processing unit (108) applying log transformation (108-2), discrete cosine transform (108-4), and cepstral liftering (108-6) to generate a compact cepstral feature representation. A classifier (110) classifies the frames as preictal or interictal, and an alert unit (112) generates seizure prediction alerts. Unlike conventional electrocardiogram-based seizure prediction systems limited by dominant cardiac activity, subject-specific variations, and wearable sensor noise, this approach achieves reliable seizure prediction through enriched seizure-specific information with significant dimensionality reduction using cepstral liftering, suitable for resource-constrained wearable devices.

title: Real-Time Seizure Prediction on an Embedded platform Using Bio-Amp EXG Pill and Feature Extraction
abstract: The present invention relates to a real-time IoMT-enabled embedded system for epileptic seizure prediction using electroencephalogram signals. The system acquires brain signals through a biopotential sensing unit and processes them using an embedded platform with intelligent feature extraction based on an interpretable multi-objective transformer framework. The system integrates multiple sensors including temperature, motion, and vibration sensors to enhance prediction accuracy. Upon detection of abnormal conditions, the system generates local alerts and transmits emergency notifications along with location information. The system further enables cloud-based monitoring and visualization for remote healthcare applications. The invention provides a portable, low-power, and efficient solution for real-time seizure prediction and patient safety.

title: Epilepsy seizure prediction using Attention based Bi-LSTM
abstract: This invention presents a real-time Epilepsy Seizure Prediction System based on an Attention-Based Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) model integrated with EEG signal-processing modules. Continuous EEG signals undergo SciPy-based preprocessing and FFT-based feature extraction to obtain temporal–frequency representations. These features are fed into an attention-enhanced Bi-LSTM network that captures bidirectional temporal dependencies while highlighting the most informative EEG segments. A classification layer generates seizure probability scores, which are visualized in real time to support early and interpretable seizure forecasting. The architecture is designed for low-latency edge deployment, enables patient-specific fine-tuning, and supports seamless clinical integration, offering a robust, efficient, and explainable solution for continuous neurological monitoring and proactive intervention.

title: “An explainable hybrid neuromorphic system for EEG-based seizure detection”
abstract: The present invention relates to an explainable hybrid neuromorphic system and method for electroencephalography (EEG)-based seizure detection is disclosed. the system comprises an EEG data acquisition and preprocessing module configured to receive single-channel EEG recordings and normalize the recordings into fixed-length segments for inference. a convolutional neural network (CNN) encoder extracts spatial-frequency features from the normalized EEG data, and a spiking neural network (SNN) temporal processing module models temporal dynamics of the extracted features using spike-based computation. a classification module classifies EEG segments into seizure-related classes, including non-seizure, interictal, and seizure states. an explainability module generates human-interpretable attribution maps that identify influential EEG temporal segments contributing to the classification decision, thereby enhancing clinical transparency and trust. a deployment interface enables exporting the hybrid CNN-SNN model for execution on low-power, resource-constrained embedded platforms. the hybrid neuromorphic architecture provides accurate, energy-efficient, and explainable seizure detection suitable for real-time and edge-based neurological monitoring applications. title: An IoT-Based Deep Learning Framework for Seizure Detection and Monitoring.
abstract: This system allows for continuous acquisition of physiological signals associated with seizures utilizing internet-based recording systems and intelligent automated analytical processes based on deep learning technology; it will allow for real-time processing of seizure detection on edge devices and cloud processing of seizure detection with long-term data records to assist in the management of epilepsy patients. The seizure detection occurs through the application of a deep learning model that identifies spatial-temporal patterns of seizure activity; upon detection of a seizure event an alert will be sent to the individual diagnosed with epilepsy and/or the epileptic patient’s caregivers or providers to notify them of the seizure event for timely intervention to take place. Both clinical and non-clinical settings May apply this framework which may provide patients more safety reduce the workload on caregivers, develop an intelligent automated monitoring system designed specifically for managing epilepsy.

title: Design of an Iterative Hybrid Causal Attention Framework with Context-Aware Meta-Learning and Bayesian Refinement for Real-Time Seizure Detection Process
abstract: ABSTRACT OF THE INVENTION: This invention presents FUSED-SEIZURE, an iterative hybrid causal attention framework for real-time seizure detection from EEG signals. The system integrates a Temporo-Spatial Transformer Graph Network (TSTG-Net) to capture complex spatial and temporal dependencies across EEG channels. A Contrastive Adversarial Embedding Module (CAEM) enhances feature discriminability using patient-specific interictal samples. The Multi-Resolution Causal Attention Network (MCAN) applies causal constraints across multiple EEG frequency bands to improve detection reliability. Real-time inference is facilitated by the Online Recursive Neuro-Bayesian Filter (ORNBF), which updates seizure probabilities recursively using lightweight neural approximators, achieving a latency of 0.42 seconds. A Temporal Meta-Learning based Patient-Specific Context (TML-PSC) module dynamically adjusts detection thresholds based on contextual factors such as medication levels, circadian rhythm, and historical seizure patterns. Evaluated on public datasets CHB-MIT and TUH, the system demonstrates 93.6% accuracy, 92.7% sensitivity, 95.1% specificity, and a false alarm rate of 0.07 per minute. The framework is designed for low-power, real-time deployment in wearable and implantable neurodevices, enabling personalized, adaptive seizure monitoring and responsive intervention. By combining causal attention, meta-learning, and Bayesian refinement, FUSED-SEIZURE addresses key limitations of existing systems and provides a robust solution for clinical neurology and patient care.

title: Enhancing Seizure Detection in EEG Signals through DWT Denoising, GAN-Based Augmentation, and Deep Learning Techniques
abstract: ABSTRACT OF THE INVENTION This invention presents an integrated multistage system for enhancing seizure detection in EEG signals through advanced preprocessing, augmentation, and deep learning techniques. The system employs Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) denoising to remove artifacts such as eye blinks and muscle movements, improving the Signal-to-Noise Ratio by 15–25%. A Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) is utilized for data augmentation, synthetically generating EEG samples to increase dataset size by 200% and address class imbalance. Spectral features are extracted using Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) and Power Spectral Density (PSD) methods, capturing seizure-related oscillations and improving classification accuracy by 10–15%. A hybrid CNN-LSTM architecture is implemented to model both spatial patterns in time-frequency representations and temporal dependencies across seizure phases, achieving 85–90% accuracy and 87% sensitivity with a 20% F1-score improvement. Furthermore, a Deep Q-Network (DQN) optimizes real-time alerting by dynamically adapting detection thresholds based on seizure probability, resulting in a 30% reduction in alert latency and a 15% increase in early detection sensitivity. The integrated approach provides a robust, noise-resistant, and clinically applicable seizure detection system that enhances diagnostic reliability, supports real-time patient monitoring, and improves intervention outcomes in epilepsy care. ________________________________________

title: EPILEPTIC SEIZURE DETECTION SYSTEM USING ENSEMBLE MACHINE LEARNING WITH BRAIN AND HEART SIGNAL ANALYSIS
abstract: The present disclosure provides an epileptic seizure detection system (5100) that includes a data acquisition module (5102) configured to acquire electroencephalogram signals from a subject, a signal preprocessing module (5110) configured to receive the acquired electroencephalogram signals and perform filtering and noise removal to generate preprocessed signals, a feature extraction module (5118) configured to extract time-domain features from the preprocessed signals, an ensemble machine learning module (5128) that includes a Random Forest classifier (5130), a Support Vector Machine classifier (5132), and a Logistic Regression classifier (5134), wherein each classifier is trained on the extracted time-domain features to classify seizure and non-seizure states, and a seizure prediction output (5142) configured to provide a seizure or non-seizure classification prediction based on combined outputs from the Random Forest classifier (5130), the Support Vector Machine classifier (5132), and the Logistic Regression classifier (5134).

title: MULTIMODAL SENSOR FUSION DEVICE FOR NON INVASIVE SILENT SEIZURE MONITORING
abstract: A non-invasive multimodal sensor fusion system intended for the identification and forecasting of quiet or non-convulsive epileptic seizures is the subject of the current invention. The gadget combines a physiological sensor suite in a smartwatch, such as heart rate (HR), electro dermal activity (EDA) and respiration rate (RR) sensors, with a piezoelectric sensor integrated into wearable eyeglasses. These multimodal biosignals are continually collected and sent to an AI- powered fusion module that examines motion signatures suggestive of seizure activity, autonomic variations, and neuromuscular micro-vibrations. The technology reduces false alarms by using contextual correlation to identify ictal, pre-ictal, and post-ictal stages using machine learning algorithms based on individual physiological patterns. The device securely archives event data on a cloud platform for clinical evaluation and sends a real-time alarm to a caregiver's smartphone when it detects odd patterns consistent with a quiet seizure. The invention offers a wearable, low- power, continuous, patient-specific monitoring solution that promotes proactive intervention for people with epilepsy, improves early seizure detection, and increases patient safety.

title: Multi-scale Depth wise separable progressive attentional knowledge distillation transfer driven for Epileptic seizure detection on EEG signals
abstract: Multi-scale Depth wise separable progressive attentional knowledge distillation transfer driven for Epileptic seizure detection on EEG signals Abstract Epilepsy, a neurological disorder caused by abnormal brain electrical activity, is difficult to diagnose and treat. This paper aims to create a KD-based deep-learning algorithm for detecting epileptic seizures. There are two primary stages: signal pre-processing and feature extraction. Initially, the focus is on denoising EEG signals to reduce errors and extract relevant information. The algorithm examines denoising methods capable of effectively removing noise and retaining essential data. The raw input data is then pre-processed to remove unwanted noises with the Upgraded Kalman Filtering (Up-KalFil) method. Wavelet Packet Decomposition (WPD) approach decomposes the original EEG signal into an approximate rhythm wave. Feature extraction plays a critical role in compressing the dimensions of the original data and capturing information reflective of EEG activity states. Time domain, frequency domain, and nonlinear dynamic features are extracted to facilitate this process. The study presents the Hierarchical Depth-wise Separable Triple Progressive Attentional Knowledge Distillation (HDSTPAKD) model and investigates the application of KD-based deep learning for detection. This model integrates teacher and student models to transfer knowledge at various depths of deep representation learning. Knowledge transfer is facilitated by a triple-attentional knowledge transfer model that combines the activation, spatial, and channel attentional frameworks. Furthermore, both the teacher and student models integrate progressive attentional modules to improve feature extraction for accurate epileptic seizure detection. Subsequently, the proposed method classifies whether the signal is healthy or affected by elliptic seizure. In the evaluation, the model attains 98.82% in the elliptic seizure recognition dataset and 99.92% in BONN dataset.

title: WEARABLE AI SYSTEM FOR REAL-TIME EPILEPTIC SEIZURE DETECTION USING MULTI-MODAL SENSOR FUSION
abstract: The present invention provides a wearable, real-time seizure detection and prediction system that integrates multi-modal physiological sensing with edge-based artificial intelligence. The device combines electrodermal activity, accelerometry, heart rate variability, electromyography, and optional EEG sensors to accurately identify tonic–clonic, focal, and absence seizures while minimizing false positives using adaptive thresholds and motion-artifact rejection. A lightweight CNN-LSTM model enables sub-second, on-device analysis without cloud dependency, and federated learning allows personalized pattern recognition while preserving patient privacy. The system further incorporates pre-seizure prediction through autonomic biomarkers and delivers closed-loop intervention via haptic feedback or transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation to potentially disrupt early seizure activity. GPS-enabled emergency alerts and a HIPAA-compliant cloud dashboard support caregiver notification and long-term clinical monitoring. This invention advances epilepsy management by combining detection, prediction, and intervention in a single, power-efficient wearable platform.

title: ADVANCED CNN–LSTM EDGE COMPUTING WEARABLE DEVICE FOR REAL-TIME EPILEPTIC SEIZURE DETECTION AND EXTENDED BATTERY LIFE
abstract: The invention relates to an advanced CNN–LSTM edge computing wearable device for real-time epileptic seizure detection and extended battery life. The device integrates EEG sensing, physiological monitoring, and an edge-deployed deep learning model to detect seizures with high accuracy and low latency. By performing all critical processing locally on the wearable platform, the system reduces power consumption, minimizes cloud dependency, and preserves data privacy. Real-time alerts are generated upon seizure detection to enable rapid medical response, making the invention a reliable and efficient solution for continuous epilepsy monitoring.

title: A STANDARDIZED ETHANOLIC EXTRACT OF ANNONA RETICULATA LEAVES AND A METHOD FOR PREVENTION AND TREATMENT OF SEIZURE AND NEUROLOGICAL DISORDERS
abstract: 7. ABSTRACT The present invention relates to a standardized ethanolic extract of Annona reticulata leaves and its use in the prevention and treatment of seizure disorders and associated neurological conditions. The extract is prepared by shade-drying and pulverizing Annona reticulata leaves followed by Soxhlet extraction using ethanol and concentration under reduced pressure to obtain a semi-solid extract rich in bioactive phytoconstituents. The extract comprises alkaloids, flavonoids, saponins, glycosides, terpenoids, tannins, carbohydrates, proteins, mucilage, and fixed oils. The extract is safe for oral administration up to 2000 mg/kg body weight and is therapeutically effective at doses of 200–400 mg/kg. Administration of the extract delays seizure onset, reduces seizure duration, and provides seizure protection by modulating excitatory–inhibitory neurotransmitter balance and enhancing endogenous antioxidant defense mechanisms. The invention provides a plant-based anticonvulsant, anxiolytic, and neuroprotective therapeutic agent with improved safety and tolerability. The figure associated with abstract is Fig. 1.

title: Epileptic Seizure Detection Using Long Short Term Memory Algorithm
abstract: ABSTRACT OF THE INVENTION Epilepsy is a neurological disorder that causes seizures to happen again and again. It is a big problem all over the world. This project presents an AI-based method for precise seizure forecasting utilizing EEG signals. Conventional algorithms frequently exhibit imprecision in identifying seizure occurrences, prompting the creation of an innovative Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model. The suggested system combines signal processing, feature extraction, and LSTM-based classification to accurately tell the difference between normal brain function and seizure activity. Validation against established methods shows that the model works better, with an amazing 99% accuracy. Because it works in real time, it can quickly find and respond to seizure events, which could lower the risks and make patients safer. This framework is a powerful tool for proactive epilepsy management because it combines advanced deep learning techniques with clinical practice. It helps patients have better outcomes and a better quality of life overall.

title: AI Based Generalised Epileptic Seizure Detection wearable System
abstract: The current innovation is a wearable safety monitoring system for older and medically susceptible people, including those with paralysis, Parkinson's disease, epilepsy, Alzheimer's disease, and other high-risk illnesses. The gadget includes a global positioning system (GPS) module for real-time location acquisition, a microphone for distress voice recognition, a heart-rate and temperature sensor for continuous physiological monitoring, and a microcontroller integrated with an accelerometer-gyroscope module for automatic detection of falls and seizure-like abnormal movements. When the system detects a fall, seizure-event indicators, abnormal vital patterns, or voice-based distress cues, it initiates emergency signaling through an audible alarm and sends alert notifications to pre-registered caregivers via wireless communication, including SMS and internet-based gateways. To facilitate manual alarm activation, there is an emergency push button. The invention's use of artificial intelligence and machine-learning algorithms to assess past and present sensor data for early seizure prediction capabilities enables proactive medical intervention. A companion smartphone application facilitates remote monitoring by displaying the patient's location in real time, physiological parameters, alert history, and predictive warnings. The device is lightweight, compact, and easy to wear all day. It runs on a rechargeable power source. This invention offers an automated, integrated, and cost-effective personal safety system that can enhance the independence of at-risk users, shorten emergency response times, and give timely assistance.

title: WEARABLE FPGA BASED VLSI ACCELERATOR FOR REAL-TIME SEIZURE FORECASTING
abstract: ABSTRACT WEARABLE FPGA BASED VLSI ACCELERATOR FOR REAL-TIME SEIZURE FORECASTING This invention presents a wearable, hardware-efficient real-time epileptic seizure forecasting device based on a CNN–LSTM deep learning accelerator deployed on FPGA/VLSI hardware. Existing seizure detection systems operate reactively and rely on high-power computing resources unsuitable for continuous wearable monitoring. The developed device addresses these limitations through hardware-optimized neural processing, quantized CNN–LSTM architectures, and parallel EEG preprocessing pipelines. The finalized wearable prototype performs continuous EEG acquisition, low-power inference, and early prediction of preictal states several minutes before seizure onset. Implemented entirely on an FPGA platform, the system achieves reduced latency, low memory usage, and energy efficiency suitable for portable medical deployment. This completed invention provides a practical, real-world hardware solution for seizure forecasting, enhancing patient safety, independence, and quality of life.

title: A DYNAMIC CROSS-MODAL MRI-GUIDED EEG MONITORING SYSTEM FOR SEIZURE DETECTION AND PREDICTION
abstract: A dynamic system integrates MRI imaging and EEG monitoring for seizure detection and prediction within the technical field of neuroimaging and neurology. The invention comprises an MRI structural biomarker processing module that acquires high-resolution MRI images and extracts quantitative anatomical biomarkers through noise filtering, normalization, and segmentation, and an adaptive EEG interpretation module that processes real-time EEG signals by applying signal conditioning, artifact suppression, and dynamic parameter adjustments. A cross-attention fusion engine performs bidirectional alignment of spatial MRI features with temporal EEG features to generate a unified multimodal representation, which is subsequently analyzed by a real-time seizure risk scoring and alerting module that computes and alerts upon exceeding a predetermined threshold, ensuring robust, patient-specific detection and prediction of seizure activity.

title: Real-time seizure detection headband
abstract: The present invention discloses a system and method for real time, ambulatory epileptic seizure detection utilizing a comfortable, non-invasive headband. The system addresses the limitations of motion-only devices by acquiring high-fidelity Electroencephalography (EEG) signals using dry electrodes. The core innovation lies in the Dual-Layer Edge AI Processing, which executes specialized algorithms to first, filter out pervasive ocular (EOG) and muscle (EMG) artifacts that mask brainwaves, and second, analyzes the cleaned EEG signal's spectral energy ratios (e.g., Theta/Delta/Alpha) to identify the characteristic high amplitude, rhythmic discharge patterns of an impending or occurring seizure. By processing data locally and achieving high specificity, the system ensures immediate, life-critical alerts are sent to caregivers with minimal latency and high reliability

title: DEVELOPMENT OF IN-EAR ELECTROENCEPHALOGRAM MONITORING AND SEIZURE DETECTION SYSTEM USING EMBEDDED ELECTRODES AND CNN GRU PIPELINE
abstract: ABSTRACT OF THE INVENTION The patent disclosure covers development of in-ear electroencephalogram monitoring and seizure detection system using embedded electrodes and CNN-GRU pipeline. The main aim is to design a compact, wearable, and intelligent neuro-monitoring device capable of capturing and analyzing brain activity in real time. The proposed system employs embedded dry electrodes integrated within ergonomically designed in-ear earbuds to acquire high-fidelity EEG signals directly from the temporal lobe, a region closely associated with epileptic activity. A low-noise analog front end and a dual-core embedded processor enable continuous signal acquisition, filtering, and digitization, ensuring medicalgrade accuracy in a non-clinical, user-friendly form factor. The recorded EEG signals are processed using a lightweight deep learning pipeline based on a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) combined with a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) architecture for robust feature extraction and temporal pattern recognition. This enables accurate detection of seizure precursors and abnormal neural activity in real time. The accompanying mobile interface provides live visualization, data logging, and alert generation to assist users and caregivers in proactive neurological management. By merging biomedical sensing, embedded hardware design, and machine learning, this system advances the development of continuous, comfortable, and intelligent EEG-based systems for early seizure detection and long-term neurological health monitoring.

title: DEEP Q LEARNING APPROACH FOR EPILEPTIC SEIZURE PREDICTION
abstract: Epilepsy affects approximately 65 million people worldwide, making it one of the most common neurological disorders. The unpredictable nature of epileptic seizures can significantly impact daily life, emphasizing the need for reliable early prediction systems. This study presents a Deep Q Network (DQN) based approach for forecasting seizures using electroencephalogram (EEG) data. The proposed model extracts essential temporal and spectral features such as mean amplitude, standard deviation, band power, and entropy to identify subtle brain activity changes that precede seizure onset. Through a reinforcement learning framework, the DQN is trained with a reward-based mechanism that reinforces accurate predictions and penalizes misclassifications, enabling adaptive learning and improved decision-making. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that the model effectively identifies seizure-prone brain states and provides advance warnings with measurable lead times. These findings suggest that reinforcement learning can play a vital role in developing intelligent, real-time EEG-based seizure prediction systems aimed at enhancing safety and quality of life for individuals with epilepsy.

title: WEARABLE CARBON–GRAPHENE NEURAL SENSING PATCH WITH AI-DRIVEN SEIZURE PREDICTION AND IOT ALERTING FRAMEWORK
abstract: The present invention relates to a seizure-prediction system (100) incorporating a flexible, skin-adherent monitoring patch (102) equipped with a carbon–graphene electrode array (104) for acquiring EEG-like neural signals. The patch integrates a signal-conditioning module (206), an analog-to-digital conversion and microcontroller unit (110), an on-device encryption module (112), a wireless communication module (208), and a thin-film lithium-ion battery (116). Encrypted neural data are transmitted to a companion mobile device (604) executing an application (122) configured for decryption and analysis. A compound neural-network engine (410), including a graph neural network, long short-term memory network, and generative adversarial network, processes the neural signals to generate seizure-risk predictions. An IoT alert distribution module (408) disseminates risk notifications to connected endpoints such as smartwatches (606), smart glasses (608), home devices (610), and automotive systems (612).

title: Neuroshield - An Epileptic Seizure Prediction Web app using EEG Signal.
abstract: Epileptic seizures refer to sudden bursts of abnormal electrical activity in the brain, often detected through EEG signals. The seizure detection and prediction are crucial for timely intervention and suitable treatment. This project investigates the integration of XAI techniques into a deep-learning EEG signal classification system for predicting epileptic seizures. The intention is to classify brain signals in three modes: ictal, interictal, and preictal, through ResNet-18 architecture with enhanced interpretability of the model. Five leading XAI methods SHAP, LIME, Grad-CAM, Integrated Gradients, and DeepLIFT were used to provide visual and quantitative insights into the predictions of the model. The performance of these techniques is assessed using various metrics, such as fidelity, localization, and stability, to determine the meaningfulness of the insights provided by the deep learning model into its own decision-making process. The dataset contained pre-recorded EEG signals classified into three seizure stages, and each sample was stored in .mat format with fixed duration. Hence no real-time signal acquisition and hardware integration exist, and data processing here is offline. A web application based on Streamlit was developed to be the frontend, which allows clinicians and users to visualize the model predictions and explanations interactively. The project aims to bring about a reconciliatory step between accuracy and interpretability of medical AI applications, thereby assuring that the system remains high- performing and interpretable in a safety-critical domain like healthcare.

title: EDGE AI-BASED SEIZURE DETECTION SYSTEM USING RASPBERRY PI
abstract: Seizures are unpredictable neurological events that require continuous monitoring to ensure patient safety and timely medical intervention. Conventional seizure detection systems often rely on centralized cloud processing or hospital-based EEG monitoring, which introduces latency, privacy concerns, and limits real-time responsiveness. This patent presents an Edge Al-based Seizure Detection System implemented on a Raspberry Pi platform for low-cost, real-time, and portable monitoring. The proposed system acquires physiological signals such as EEG and accelerometer data through wearable or non-invasive sensors. The data are preprocessed locally using digital filters to remove noise and artifacts, followed by feature extraction in both the time and frequency domains. A lightweight deep learning model—optimized for edge deployment is used to classify seizure and non-seizure events directly on the Raspberry Pi without reliance on cloud servers. Upon detection, the system triggers alerts via mobile notification or IoT dashboard to caregivers and healthcare providers. Experimental results demonstrate that the edge-deployed model achieves high accuracy with minimal latency while maintaining low power consumption, making it suitable for continuous home or ambulatory monitoring. The integration of Edge Al with a Raspberry Pi ensures patient data privacy, reduced dependency on network connectivity, and real-time decision-making. This work illustrates the feasibility of an affordable, intelligent, and portable seizure detection system that supports proactive epilepsy management and improved quality of life for patients.
